tests.stimulus: Initialize all native inputs to zero at time zero, generate a 10 ns clock, then drive inputs on each falling edge and retain them through the next rising edge. Randomize each input over its full declared two-state width; whenever G is true, force rs2_data[64]=0 and fp_val=0 for ctrl_is_std, and restrict fp_val=1 to uopc=1 or 2. Toggle reset and all native inputs, exercise active and inactive G, and preserve asserted legal constraints at each rising edge.
tests.expected: The complete native ALUExeUnit interface has no parameters or functional storage. Outputs react combinationally to current inputs; compare after propagation has settled. clock only checks legality on its rising edge. reset disables those legality checks but does not reset, clear or gate functional outputs. All described outputs remain defined for legal two-state inputs, including when corresponding valid is low. Numerical results with X/Z inputs are unspecified. Let G mean io_req_valid and bit 2 of io_req_bits_uop_fu_code. When reset is low at a rising edge, G and ctrl_is_std require rs2_data[64]=0 and fp_val=0; G and fp_val require uopc=1 or 2.
tests.checker: Sample actual and independent model outputs 2 ns after each falling-edge drive, before the next rising edge. Compare all output bits using four-state !== against the same input-only dvbench_model; count 4096 observations and fail on any mismatch or a vacuous run.
